[Thinking]
**Exploring Modular Extensions**

My current focus is on extending the modularity results presented by BHKRY. I'm investigating how to apply these principles specifically to the $U(1,1)$ case, which was omitted in their original work, by exploring embedding techniques for its Shimura varieties.

**Proving Modularity for U(1,1)**

I am extending modularity results to the $U(1,1)$ case. My current efforts involve relating genus 1 curves to $U(n-1, 1)$ Shimura varieties and establishing a precise pullback formula for generating series of arithmetic divisors. This will then allow me to prove the $U(1,1)$ modularity.

**Refining Prooftokens**

I'm refining some proof-related terminology. I've identified and corrected several minor typos, such as changing "ofther" to "of the" and "inhten" to "in the." I'm also solidifying "proovehten" as "prove the" within the context of modularity results.
[/Thinking]

This paper is a complement of the modularity result of Bruinier, Howard, Kudla, Rapoport and Yang (BHKRY) for the special case $U(1,1)$ not considered there. The main idea is to embed a $U(1, 1)$ Shimura curve to many $U(n-1, 1)$ Shimura varieties for big $n$, and prove a precise pullback formula of the generating series of arithmetic divisors. Afterwards, we use the modularity result of BHKRY together with the existence of non-vanishing of classical theta series at any given point in the upper half plane to prove the modularity result on $U(1, 1)$ Shimura curves.
